text:
perf-bot: [ALERT] Nightly perf dashboard: p99 latency +38% on canary-gpu-pool since 04:00 UTC. Spike correlates with merge PR #4321.
maya: saw this on dashboards, looks like kernel-selector change landed yesterday.
liam: I started a bisect on the canary branch, first suspect is the adaptive-handoff-threshold change in runtime/selector.go
sarah: CI perf job 12f7 failed with 8% tail regressions earlier, link: https://ci.redwood/suite/12f7
maya: can we pin canary to last-good (deploy-tag: 2026-03-16-canary) until we bisect? :thumbsup:
liam: ok pinning now, running quick smoke. /deploy pin canary 2026-03-16-canary
ops-bot: deployment pinned to 2026-03-16-canary by liam
maya: while bisecting, added perf profile capture (ux: pprof + nvprof) for a few troublesome instances
liam: found that kernel selection now prefers large-atten kernels for short sequences because of heuristic misweighting
sarah: reproducer: run bench with seq=64 batch=8 model=gpt-small; we see context switch overheads spike after ~2000 tokens
liam: attaching snippet of offending diff:
```
- if (score > threshold) choose_large_kernel();
+ if (score >= threshold - epsilon) choose_large_kernel(); // PR #4321
```
maya: epsilon was to stabilize noisy scores, but looks like it made selector too eager. Could explain higher latency for short sequences.
sarah: can we test reverting that line in a canary build? I can run quick build+smoke
liam: running local revert + smoke now, ETA 12m
maya: created rollback PR #4330 to revert the epsilon change, requesting quick review @eng-runtime
perf-bot: CI perf job 12g started for revert PR #4330
liam: smoke looks promising, p99 reduced back to baseline in quick test :tada:
perf-bot: CI perf job 12g completed, tail metrics within 1% of baseline
maya: merging rollback and will kick a new nightly canary run
sarah: follow up: we should add a small unit test for selector boundary and add perf-tester job to catch this class of regressions
maya: agreed, filing a follow-up ticket: https://issues.redwood/INF-987
liam: thanks all, keeping eyes on nightdash, will reopen if anything else pops up :eyes:
